stories.headline: Why is Maharashtra experiencing an earthquake swarm? | Explained
stories.title: Why is Maharashtra experiencing an earthquake swarm? | Explained
stories.summary: There has been a spate of small earthquakes in Maharashtra over the last fortnight; seismologists call this pattern of quakes an earthquake swarm, and Maharashtra has experienced them often before
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: There has been a spate of small earthquakes in Maharashtra over the last fortnight, according to local reports.
Of the 29 tremors during this period, 24 were in and around Nashik, four were in Palghar and one was in Nagpur.
They weren’t particularly strong — the strongest was in Nagpur on August 8, of magnitude 4.3 — although they were also shallow, around 5-8 km deep.
Seismologists call this pattern of quakes an earthquake swarm, and Maharashtra has experienced them often before.
An earthquake is a sudden movement of rocks along a fault, i.e. a fracture or a region of weakness in the earth’s crust.
In some places, friction can prevent two rock blocks from sliding past each other.

stories.headline: Students raise ₹2.5 lakh to help flood-hit families in Kumarakom
stories.title: Students raise ₹2.5 lakh to help flood-hit families in Kumarakom
stories.summary: Students crowdfunding raised ₹2.5 lakh for flood-hit families, distributing 84 relief kits containing food and essentials via The Tiny Seed.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: In a display of empathy and leadership, a group of high school students has raised ₹2.5 lakh through crowdfunding to aid families devastated by the recent floods in Kumarakom.
The initiative was driven by Class 11 students from Pallikoodam School in Kalathippady, a student from Excelsior School in Illickal, and two students from Dubai Millennium School.
Partnering with the Kottayam-based non-profit organisation, The Tiny Seed, these young changemakers successfully mobilised resources to support those in need.
The funds were used to compile and distribute relief kits to 84 flood-affected families of students studying at the Kumarakom Government Vocational Higher Secondary School (GVHSS).
Many of these families had been displaced from their waterlogged homes and were seeking temporary shelter at relief camps set up on the school campus.
Each carefully curated relief kit was designed to help families rebuild their daily lives.
The packages contained vital food supplies such as rice, sugar, and pulses, alongside essential toiletries, cleaning products, bath towels, and bedsheets.
The distribution of the relief kits took place at the school, in the presence of Government High School Headmaster.
A Abdul Kalam, Higher Secondary Principal T Sathyan, and VHSE Principal MS Bijesh.
Their support underscored the communal solidarity backing the young students' proactive initiative.
Through their efforts, these school students have demonstrated that age is no barrier to making a meaningful social impact.

By coming together across different schools and even international borders, they have written a beautiful new chapter in compassion and social responsibility, proving how a collective effort can bring immense relief to struggling communities.

stories.headline: NIA court issues non-bailable warrant against Pak-based LeT commander
stories.title: NIA court issues non-bailable warrant against Pak-based LeT commander
stories.summary: Jammu, Aug 18: A special NIA court in Jammu has issued a non-bailable warrant against operational commander of Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) for his involvement in terror activities in Jammu and Kashmir, officials said on Tuesday. The non-bailable warrant (NBW) was issued last month against absconding accused Mohammad Yaqoob, a designated terrorist of Pakistani origin who is also known by the aliases Abu Sumama, SumamaIlyas and Waris Ali, the officials said, citing an order issued by the NIA court. Yaqoob is the second top LeT terrorist against whom the NIA court in Jammu has issued an NBW since July 8. Earlier, the special NIA court had issued NBW against Hafiz Saeed, the Pakistan-based chief of the proscribed terror outfit, in connection with the Pahalgam terror attack case. Yaqoob was among 23 individuals designated as terrorists by the Union Home Ministry on July 4. He operates as anLeT operational commander based in Islamabad (ChattaBakhtawar) and also coordinates financial and logistical support for other LeT cadres active in Kashmir to carry out terrorist activities in India. According to the court order dated July 16, the officials said the warrant was sought by the NIA against Yaqoob, who is listed as a designated terrorist under Section 35 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, in connection with an ongoing investigation in a case registered under UAPA, Arms Act and Explosive Substances Act at a police station in Srinagar. The case stems from the arrest of a motorcyclist Mohammad Naqeeb Bhat at Gujar Tent, Pandach and recovery of a Chinese grenade and 15 live rounds early this year. Bhat's arrest led to the busting of a major terror network spread across different states of the country and arrest of four more terrorists including two Pakistani nationals -- Abdullah Rajput alias Kamran Ahmed and Khubaib alias Usman Jatt. The NIA told the court that investigation had revealed the involvement of Pakistan-based handler Mohammad Yaqoob, based on material collected and disclosures made by the arrested terrorists. The agency said Yaqoob had provided directions to the arrested accused to carry out terrorist activities in the Valley, including attacks on security forces and civilians. After examining the application and record, the court observed that the accused was at large and that the investigating agency had been unable to secure his attendance through ordinary means, the officials said.

stories.headline: A year of Trump tariffs, India’s US exports firm
stories.title: A year of Trump tariffs, India’s US exports firm
stories.summary: India’s share of exports to the US remained largely unchanged despite a year of President Donald Trump’s punitive tariffs and New Delhi’s efforts to diversify its trade with a raft of new deals with other countries. An analysis of trade ministry data for the 12 months through July shows the US continues to account for about 20% of India’s exports. Over that period, Trump slapped tariffs as high as 50% on Indian goods at one point, before dropping it to 18% in February this year. The goods now carry a 10% tariff rate.Also Read| India widens export basket: Amrapali mangoes, premium cherries, frozen French fries find new marketThe uncertainty in US-India trade relations prompted Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government to expedite free trade negotiations with other major markets. In the past year, India has inked a trade deal with the UK, which took effect in July, as well as agreements with the European Union, Oman and New Zealand.133338340While that diversification push has continued, with exporters scouting newer markets to reduce risk, the US share has remained resilient, underscoring the difficulty of replacing the world’s largest economy. It will take at least two to three years for market diversification to show meaningful results, said Ajay Sahai, director general of the Federation of Indian Export Organizations, adding that the US continues to be the most attractive market. The share of exports to the US has grown to nearly 20% from 17.4% in 2022-23, official data show.All the same, “the industry has become extremely cautious of the fact that they have to diversify as a strategy to de-risk,” Sahai said. “And from that perspective, I think it’s a very good lesson the US tariff war taught us.”India has also broadly maintained its share of exports to other major markets, data for the 12 months through July showed. Trade TalksThe sheer scale and appetite of the US for a broad range of Indian goods make it a uniquely important market, particularly for electronics, engineering goods, pharmaceuticals, gems and jewelry and textiles. The two countries have yet to sign a trade deal, despite months of high-level talks. Indian officials are working to shift the balance by expanding the number of markets where exporters can compete on favorable terms. The government has also sought to broaden the range of goods sold overseas, adding about 500 new product lines, mainlyinelectronics, engineering and marine products.Also Read| India must strengthen shipping capacity, naval protection amid growing chokepoints: GTRI“The focus is on engaging with economies that collectively account for over two-thirds of global GDP,” Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal told Bloomberg News last week when asked about the government’s trade diversification strategy.“In an environment of global uncertainty and shifting trade patterns, FTAs also serve as institutional anchors for trusted economic partnerships,” Agrawal said referring to Free Trade Agreements. He said the deals aim to reduce reliance on any single market and strengthen trade ties.Earlier this month, India signed terms of reference with the Southern African Customs Union to accelerate trade negotiations. New Delhi is seeking to extend that network across Latin America, the Middle East and Africa. 133338353Trade agreements already in force have meanwhile begun to show evidence of a potential payoff.India now counts Australia among its faster-growing markets, while the UAE was its second-biggest export destination in the 12 months through July. Both countries signed trade agreements with India in 2022.133338362Several smaller destinations are growing rapidly, though from bases that remain a fraction of the US market. In the 12 months through July, nations including Tanzania, Vietnam, South Korea, Sri Lanka, and Kenya were among the markets showing solid growth. Exports to China have also accelerated, surging 42% in the 12 months through July, according to Bloomberg calculations based on the official figures. India shipped goods worth $21.5 billion to the Asian giant in the period, compared with $88.5 billion to the US. Pritam Banerjee, a trade analyst and former head of think tank Centre for WTO Studies, said free trade pacts can become a catalyst for shifting manufacturing away from China but warned that India’s window of opportunity is narrow.Deeper integration with Group of 20 nations, which represent 85% of global GDP, along with countries in Latin America, the Middle East and Africa, would help India immensely in that shift, he said.

opening: India’s share of exports to the US remained largely unchanged despite a year of President Donald Trump’s punitive tariffs and New Delhi’s efforts to diversify its trade with a raft of new deals with other countries.
An analysis of trade ministry data for the 12 months through July shows the US continues to account for about 20% of India’s exports.
body: Over that period, Trump slapped tariffs as high as 50% on Indian goods at one point, before dropping it to 18% in February this year.
The goods now carry a 10% tariff rate.
The uncertainty in US-India trade relations prompted Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government to expedite free trade negotiations with other major markets.
In the past year, India has inked a trade deal with the UK, which took effect in July, as well as agreements with the European Union, Oman and New Zealand.

While that diversification push has continued, with exporters scouting newer markets to reduce risk, the US share has remained resilient, underscoring the difficulty of replacing the world’s largest economy.

It will take at least two to three years for market diversification to show meaningful results, said Ajay Sahai, director general of the Federation of Indian Export Organizations, adding that the US continues to be the most attractive market.
All the same, “the industry has become extremely cautious of the fact that they have to diversify as a strategy to de-risk,” Sahai said.

“And from that perspective, I think it’s a very good lesson the US tariff war taught us.” India has also broadly maintained its share of exports to other major markets, data for the 12 months through July showed.
Trade Talks.

The sheer scale and appetite of the US for a broad range of Indian goods make it a uniquely important market, particularly for electronics, engineering goods, pharmaceuticals, gems and jewelry and textiles.
The two countries have yet to sign a trade deal, despite months of high-level talks.
Indian officials are working to shift the balance by expanding the number of markets where exporters can compete on favorable terms.
The government has also sought to broaden the range of goods sold overseas, adding about 500 new product lines, mainlyinelectronics, engineering and marine products.

“The focus is on engaging with economies that collectively account for over two-thirds of global GDP,” Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal told Bloomberg News last week when asked about the government’s trade diversification strategy.
“In an environment of global uncertainty and shifting trade patterns, FTAs also serve as institutional anchors for trusted economic partnerships,” Agrawal said referring to Free Trade Agreements.
He said the deals aim to reduce reliance on any single market and strengthen trade ties.
Earlier this month, India signed terms of reference with the Southern African Customs Union to accelerate trade negotiations.
New Delhi is seeking to extend that network across Latin America, the Middle East and Africa.
133338353Trade agreements already in force have meanwhile begun to show evidence of a potential payoff.
India now counts Australia among its faster-growing markets, while the UAE was its second-biggest export destination in the 12 months through July.
Both countries signed trade agreements with India in 2022.
Several smaller destinations are growing rapidly, though from bases that remain a fraction of the US market.
In the 12 months through July, nations including Tanzania, Vietnam, South Korea, Sri Lanka, and Kenya were among the markets showing solid growth.
India shipped goods worth $21.5 billion to the Asian giant in the period, compared with $88.5 billion to the US.

Pritam Banerjee, a trade analyst and former head of think tank Centre for WTO Studies, said free trade pacts can become a catalyst for shifting manufacturing away from China but warned that India’s window of opportunity is narrow.
Deeper integration with Group of 20 nations, which represent 85% of global GDP, along with countries in Latin America, the Middle East and Africa, would help India immensely in that shift, he said.

stories.headline: Report on illegal mining submitted in NGT
stories.title: Report on illegal mining submitted in NGT
stories.summary: A report submitted by the Joint Committee (JC) comprising top officials from Ministry of Environment Forest & Climate Change -MoEFCC, Central Pollution Control Board -CPCB & J&K Pollution Control Committee -JKPCC along with Deputy Commissioners of Budgam and Pulwama have confirmed that large-scale illegal earth mining in the karewas of Pulwama and Budgam in last 5 years. The report mentioned that more than 18 lakh metric tons of clay ,sand , gravel has been illegally looted in Zadoora , Gowherpora and Rangeen Kultreh villages of Pulwama and Budgam districts. Out of 18 lakh MTs , 13 lakh MTs of material has been excavated from Gowherpora and Rangeen Kultreh villages of Chadoora Budgam and around 5 lakhs MTs from Zadoora village of Pulwama in Hastikhud area. These reports were placed on record before National Green Tribunal-NGT on Monday 17th August 2026 in the case of Raja Muzaffar Bhat v/s J&K Government and others case. The counsel for the Government as well as petitioner Dr Raja Muzaffar Bhat sought time to file their responses and the case is now listed for hearing on November 4. The reports signed and submitted by Member Secretary J&K Pollution Control Committee , Director CPCB, MoEF & DCs of Pulwama and Budgam has clearly mentioned that large scale illegal excavation has taken place between 2019-2024 in Zadoora and Gowherpora villages of Pulwama and Budgam District. The report quoting Mining Department J&K Govt mentions that illegal excavation work took place due to law and order situation post article 370 abrogation and COVID 19 pandemic in 2020 and 2021. On page 4 of the report dated 12.6.2026 the Member Secretary J&K Pollution Control Committee -JKPCC Dr R Gopinath makes some glaring revelations with regard to Gowherpora site where NKC Projects Pvt Ltd has been excavating clay, sand and bajri from 2021 to 2024 . The relevant para reads: “It was observed that Environmental Clearance has not been obtained prior to commencement of mining activities. The earth mining was carried out without approved mining plan, consent from Pollution Control Committee and Environmental Management Plan (EMP) and Environmental Clearance-EC”. In Zadoora Hastikhud area loot and plunder has taken place and this has been reported by the joint committee in its report. The report filed by Director Ecology, Environment and Remote Sensing also confirms large scale mining as they have placed on record satellite imagery between 2014 to 2026. The said report submitted before National Green Tribunal -NGT reads: “Government is trying to take benefit of article 370 abrogation and COVID 19 pandemic and it is a known fact that there was complete curfew and lockdown during these times and no movement of traffic was allowed. There were security forces on every major road in villages and towns and how come the Mining Department or other Government authorities claim loot and plunder took place during that time? 18 lakh MTs is a very small amount. This is 100 times more, I am sure. I will take up this case with NGT as well as anti corruption agencies like CBI or ACB. The Govt officials who allowed this loot will be identified” said Dr Raja Muzaffar Bhat. Pertinently a joint inspection team was constituted by the National Green Tribunal (NGT), comprising senior officials from the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) and the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), J&K Pollution Control Committee- JKPCC , DCs of Pulwama and Budgam early this year. This team had visited Zadoora in Pulwama and Gowherpora, Rangeen Kultreh in Chadoora, Budgam in April this year to assess allegations of illegal earth mining. The report was submitted in NGT recently. “The case is now crystal clear, the reports of NGTs joint committee , JK Pollution Control Committee have clearly exposed the illegal mining done in karewas of Budgam and Pulwama. The company called NKC Projects Pvt Ltd has looted our streams and rivers and has been imposed with Environmental Compensation -EC in Shaliganga case. In the Sukhnag case also they will be penalised and now I urge upon Chairman JKPCC to impose EC on them in this case as well and make sure the company is blacklisted as well. This company has not done any development but they caused disaster and looted sand , clay , gravel , boulders worth hundreds of crores which needs a high level probe” Dr Raja Muzaffar added.

stories.headline: India vs Pakistan Hockey World Cup: Ashok Kumar recalls the goal that won India the 1975 final
stories.title: India vs Pakistan Hockey World Cup: Ashok Kumar recalls the goal that won India the 1975 final
stories.summary: As India and Pakistan renew their Hockey World Cup rivalry after 16 years, revisit Ashok Kumar’s first-person account of the 1975 final, when his goal gave India its only men’s Hockey World Cup title.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'world cup' in title weight 42
event term: 'world cup' in summary weight 25.2
article_sentences: India and Pakistan meet at the Hockey World Cup on Wednesday, August 19, for the first time in 16 years.

Ahead of the latest chapter in one of hockey’s fiercest rivalries, Sportstar revisits this first-person account by Ashok Kumar, who scored India’s winning goal in the 1975 World Cup final in Kuala Lumpur.

Written as a reflection on India’s journey through the tournament, Ashok recalls the tense semifinal against host Malaysia, the final against Pakistan and the moment that became the defining goal of his career.
In his own words, he takes us back to the campaign that gave India its first men’s Hockey World Cup title and remains the country’s only World Cup triumph.
It is vivid.
The whole journey, from the time we assembled for the tournament to returning home to a rousing welcome.
It was one of the finest moments of Indian hockey.
Kuala Lumpur shall always remain a memorable venue for all of us.
Beating Pakistan in the final was the most emphatic statement we could have ever made.
Needless to say, there was tension before the match, but once the ball began rolling we knew we had a job in hand.
That we accomplished it with some sensational play was a tribute to the hard work of every member of that wonderful Indian team.

stories.summary: The Supreme Court has ordered an independent examination of allegations involving loan transactions, fund diversion and other suspected financial irregularities.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Tuesday directed the CBI to independently examine allegations of financial irregularities against Indiabulls Housing Finance Ltd and its associated entities, including transactions earlier examined by the Delhi.
Police Economic Offences Wing (EOW).
The Court said the CBI would not be guided by the EOW’s conclusions while examining the allegations.

A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant and comprising Justice Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued the directions while hearing a PIL filed by Citizens Whistleblower Forum, which has alleged suspicious loan transactions, diversion of funds, manipulation of share prices and evergreening of loans involving Indiabulls-linked entities.
The direction came after the petitioner questioned the EOW’s decision not to proceed further on five of the transactions.
The Court noted that the EOW had already examined those allegations and had opined that further investigation was not advisable.
Since the petitioner was challenging the EOW’s conclusions and seeking an independent investigation, the Supreme Court directed the CBI to examine the allegations irrespective of the EOW’s report.
Senior Advocate Prashant Bhushan, appearing for the petitioner, submitted that an RBI circular requires bank frauds involving amounts above ₹50 crore to be investigated by the CBI.
He argued that the material referred to in the ED complaint disclosed prima facie allegations of fraud, criminal conspiracy, diversion of funds and evergreening involving public money.
“The EOW is not the competent authority to investigate such bank-fraud allegations,” Bhushan submitted.
He argued that the CBI had not investigated the five allegations because the EOW was already looking into them.
According to Bhushan, the petitioner wanted one competent agency to independently examine the allegations instead of relying on the EOW’s conclusions.

article_sentences: Guwahati: The Assam Cabinet has approved the enactment of the Assam Private Coaching Institutes (Control and Student Mental Health Safeguard) Rules, 2026, Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said.
Under the new framework, private coaching institutes with 50 or more students will be required to obtain mandatory registration.
The District Commissioner of the respective district will serve as the competent authority for implementing the registration process.

Registered coaching institutes will be required to renew their registration annually and submit infrastructure safety certificates as part of the compliance requirements, according to the Chief Minister.

The rules also require institutes to comply with prescribed student mental health safeguards and infrastructure standards under the National Building Code (NBC), as well as applicable norms of the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) and the University Grants Commission (UGC).
In addition, coaching institutes will have to provide proof that a qualified counsellor has been engaged to support students’ mental health and well-being.
The measures aim to bring private coaching institutes under a regulatory framework while strengthening student safety, infrastructure standards and mental health support.

stories.headline: Ex-Lok Sabha MP Moves Supreme Court For Fixation Of MSP Based On Swaminathan Commission Report, Crop Loan Waiver
stories.title: Ex-Lok Sabha MP Moves Supreme Court For Fixation Of MSP Based On Swaminathan Commission Report, Crop Loan Waiver
stories.summary: Petitioner-Vadde Rao seeks one-time waiver of crop loan dues of small and marginal farmers affected by agrarian distress.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Petitioner-Vadde Rao seeks one-time waiver of crop loan dues of small and marginal farmers affected by agrarian distress.

A PIL has been filed before the Supreme Court seeking implementation of a legally enforceable Minimum Support Price (MSP) for all notified agricultural crops based on C2 (actual cost of cultivation) plus 50 percent (profit margin) formula in terms of the recommendations of the Swaminathan Commission.

The plea, filed by farmer and former Member of Lok Sabha Vadde Sobhanadreeswara Rao, also seeks formulation of a timebound debt relief mechanism, which may include a one-time waiver of crop loan dues of small and marginal farmers affected by agrarian distress.
A bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana today tagged the petition with a similar case.

Briefly put, the petitioner, besides the above, seeks directions to the respondent-authorities to formulate in a timebound manner a statutory framework to ensure that no agricultural produce is procured below the MSP.
He further prays for a direction to the respondents to consider framing a central legislation on the lines of the Kerala Farmers' Debt Relief Commission Act.
- Immediate relief to distressed farmers, such as moratorium on recovery of agricultural loans in cases of crop failures and natural calamities.

In April, the Supreme Court issued notice on the plea of 3 Maharashtra-based farmers seeking directions to the Union to give due weightage to C2, the exact cost of cultivation, while fixing MSP for agricultural produce.

stories.headline: Assam Cabinet Clears Major Reforms on Child Protection, Student Mental Health and Youth
stories.title: Assam Cabinet Clears Major Reforms on Child Protection, Student Mental Health and Youth
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet clears' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Thrust on child protection, juvenile justice, oil and gas exploration, allotment of land for IIM, a rule regarding mental health safeguards in private coaching centres, etc.

GUWAHATI: The state cabinet took several important decisions relating to child protection, juvenile justice, oil and gas exploration, allotment of land for IIM, a rule regarding mental health safeguards in private coaching centres, etc.

Speaking to the media after the cabinet meeting, the Chief Minister said, "The State Cabinet has approved the enactment of the Assam Private Coaching Institutes (Control and Student Mental Health Safeguard) Rules, 2026.

The mandatory registration framework of the says (a) any institute with 50+ students must register, (b) the District Commissioner serves as the competent authority, and (c) compliance with student mental health norms."
The Chief Minister said, "Many students commit suicide in private coaching centres for not being able to sustain the load of course material.
Such coaching centres should have psychologists to counsel these students.

The Chief Minister said, "The cabinet has approved the Assam Hydrocarbon Exploration, Production and Upstream Ecosystem Development Policy, 2026, with a validity of five years from the date of its notification.
In the past 20 years, there has been no new exploration of oil and gas in Assam.
Many companies are reluctant to evince interest in drilling, as in the event of not finding oil reserves, they may incur loss.
To attract their interest, we will provide incentives, along with logistic support, through this policy.

To optimise administrative efficiency, the State Cabinet has approved amendments to the Assam Social Welfare (Recruitment and Promotion) Service Orders, 1994, regarding cadre restructuring, creation of new cadres, promotion criteria, and streamlining of promotion processes, he said, adding that to ensure safety, security, dignity and well-being of children, the State Cabinet has approved the Assam State Child Protection Policy, 2026, as a commitment towards effective implementation of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, and POCSO Rules, 2020.
The policy will help to establish a uniform, statewide protection protocol across public and private entities caring for children.

stories.headline: Goa Government Moves Supreme Court Seeking Life Sentence For Tarun Tejpal In Rape Case
stories.title: Goa Government Moves Supreme Court Seeking Life Sentence For Tarun Tejpal In Rape Case
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Goa government has approached the Supreme Court seeking enhancement of the sentence imposed on former Tehelka editor Tarun Tejpal in the 2013 rape case, asking that he be sentenced to life imprisonment instead of the 10-year rigorous imprisonment awarded by the Bombay High Court.
The State clarified it challenges only the quantum of punishment and does not seek to reopen or question the findings of conviction recorded by the High Court.
The Bombay High Court's Goa bench, comprising Justices Neela Gokhale and Amit Jamsandekar, had on August 6 overturned Tejpal's acquittal by the trial court and convicted him in the 2013 case.
The court subsequently sentenced him to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment.
The High Court had noted that the incident took place 13 years ago and that there was no report of any subsequent criminal misconduct by Tejpal.
It consequently declined the Goa government's request for the maximum punishment of life imprisonment and imposed the minimum sentence prescribed for the rape conviction.
The case arose from allegations that Tejpal sexually assaulted a junior colleague inside an elevator at a luxury hotel in Goa during an event organised by Tehelka in November 2013.
The Goa Sessions Court had acquitted him in 2021, following which the State challenged the acquittal before the Bombay High Court.
The High Court convicted Tejpal under provisions of the Indian Penal Code relating to rape, sexual harassment and assault with intent to disrobe.
The rape provision under which he was convicted carried a minimum punishment of 10 years and permitted a sentence extending to life imprisonment.

stories.headline: Websol Drops Andhra Pradesh for Its Proposed Cell & Module Plant, Bets On Bengal
stories.title: Websol Drops Andhra Pradesh for Its Proposed Cell & Module Plant, Bets On Bengal
stories.summary: Indian solar cell and module manufacturing company Websol Energy System has shifted the proposed location of its Phase 3 solar manufacturing expansion from Andhra Pradesh to West Bengal, with the company now in the process of securing land near its existing manufacturing facility at Falta. The move is perhaps the clearest sign of the difference a change in government at the local state level has meant in Bengal. Vikram Solar, another solar giant in Bengal had chosen to move out and expand in Tamil Nadu when the previous TMC government held power in the state. This also marks another example of solar companies shifting project sites or what they often describe as a “restructuring of plans.” after shopping for the best offer from states. Earlier, Waaree Energies, which had planned a 6 GW integrated ingot-to-module manufacturing facility in Dhenkanal, Odisha, and later decided to exit the eastern state and focus on states such as Gujarat and Maharashtra for its expansion plans. Websol’s latest move appears to be another example of a similar exercise. Factors including faster project execution, better infrastructure, lower costs, or greater hand-holding and support from state governments often are seen as key driving forces behind such moves. Websol Keeps 4 GW Expansion Plan Intact Despite the change in location, Websol has maintained that there is no change in its overall expansion plans, project cost or funding strategy and remains confident of executing its planned 4 GW capacity expansion in phases. The location change was one of the key issues discussed during Websol’s Q1 FY27 earnings call, with investors seeking clarity on why the company had moved away from its earlier plan for an expansion at Naidupeta in Andhra Pradesh. Websol spent roughly six months preparing for the Andhra Pradesh route, including an MoU and approval, before deciding that its existing West Bengal ecosystem offered better execution synergies. Management acknowledged the time spent in Andhra Pradesh but said it believes the move is ultimately better for the organisation. Websol management said the decision was primarily driven by the operating synergies it expects to derive from expanding around its existing manufacturing base in West Bengal. The company has been operating in the state for more than three decades and believes the existing ecosystem can help it execute the next phase of capacity expansion more efficiently. “We felt that doing it here we will be able to get the requisite synergies on account of supply chain, manpower, and just be able to execute faster in general,” Executive Director Sanjana Khaitan said during the call. The company has clarified that its planned expansion is 4 GW in total and will be implemented in two phases of 2 GW each, rather than 4 GW each of cell and module capacity. Management said the phased approach is intended to help manage technology and execution risks. From Andhra Pradesh To Falta The proposed Phase 3 facility was earlier planned at Naidupeta in Andhra Pradesh. There had been no financial outflow towards the Andhra Pradesh land, according to the company. Websol said the preparatory work around the project, including the layout, equipment and identification of the team, had already been completed. The company expects land approval during Q2 FY27, potentially in August. Construction is expected to begin around mid-September and take approximately nine months. Equipment ordering is planned around December, with machinery expected to reach the facility around April-May, followed by about two months of trial runs. Websol has maintained that the shift in location should not change the broader project timeline. “The capacity we have announced is what we are confident of executing. Our project cost also remains the same, and the funding strategy and the pathway to that, which we have previously discussed also remains the same,” Khaitan said. Cost And Operational Synergies The company expects the West Bengal location to provide both cost and operational benefits. Management indicated that land-related expenditure is expected to be lower compared with Andhra Pradesh. It also expects equipment costs to have declined over time, potentially reducing the overall project cost. In addition, Websol expects to require fewer new employees, particularly at the senior level, because it can leverage skilled manpower already available at its existing facility. “Establishing the expansion in our home state provides us with significant synergies in terms of infrastructure, availability of skilled manpower, supply chain and operational resources,” the company said. The decision comes as Websol seeks to build its next phase of capacity around an existing manufacturing base rather than establish an entirely separate operating ecosystem. Existing Cell, Module Capacity Runs At High Utilisation The location change also comes at a time when Websol’s existing cell and module manufacturing operations are operating at significantly higher utilisation. In Q1 FY27, Websol produced 259 MW of solar cells compared with 126 MW in the year-ago quarter. Cell utilisation reached 92%. Module production more than doubled to 103 MW from 50 MW, while module utilisation increased to 81% from 39% a year earlier. Management said both businesses are now operating close to full effective utilisation, although the TOPCon upgrade could result in some temporary downtime. The higher utilisation translated into revenue from operations of ₹373 crore, up 70% year-on-year from ₹219 crore. EBITDA increased 21% to ₹126 crore, while profit after tax rose 16% to ₹78 crore. However, the increase in module production has changed Websol’s product mix. Since module margins are lower than cell margins, the company’s EBITDA margin declined to 34% in Q1 FY27 from 47% in the corresponding quarter last year, even as absolute EBITDA increased. Management said its objective is to operate the entire manufacturing base efficiently, grow absolute earnings and cash generation, and improve the economics of the business over time. Demand Remains Strong In DCR Market Websol’s confidence in adding manufacturing capacity is also linked to its focus on the domestic content requirement market. The company said its products are supplied largely to DCR projects, particularly those linked to the PM Surya Ghar and PM-KUSUM programmes, and that it is not currently seeing a reduction in demand from these segments. Management also expects the broader solar market to continue expanding, citing emerging demand from artificial intelligence and data centres, battery energy storage systems and the growing requirement for solar-plus-storage capacity. This demand outlook is supporting Websol’s confidence in scaling both its cell and module manufacturing operations. ₹1,278 Crore Order Book As of June 30, Websol had a confirmed order book of ₹1,278 crore, compared with ₹1,161 crore at the end of March 2026. The company said this provides visibility into operations for the next few quarters. Websol, however, only includes firm purchase orders in its disclosed order book. The company does not count recurring business from customers that regularly purchase its products without entering into fixed-term contracts. Management said it continues to receive regular inquiries for solar cells and modules in the DCR market and remains focused on producing and supplying to its regular customers. The company also indicated that it has sufficient order visibility to sell the production it is generating, although the mix between cell and module sales can vary from quarter to quarter depending on realisations and market conditions. TOPCon Upgrade Ahead Of Larger Expansion Before the larger greenfield expansion, Websol is upgrading one of its existing Mono PERC cell lines to TOPCon. The upgrade will increase the line’s capacity from 600 MW to 750 MW, adding approximately 150 MW of capacity. The project is expected to be completed by March 2027 and involves estimated capital expenditure of around ₹270 crore. Management expects the investment to have a payback period of two to three years. The company expects TOPCon to generate incremental revenue through higher wattage per cell, higher efficiency and higher realisation compared with Mono PERC. Management said the wattage per cell could rise from around 7.6-7.7 Wp for its current Mono PERC cells to more than 9.5 Wp for TOPCon. Websol also views the conversion as a learning exercise ahead of its larger greenfield expansion, giving the company practical experience in TOPCon technology before it ramps up the planned new capacity. 4 GW Expansion To Be Executed In Phases The larger expansion remains central to Websol’s growth strategy. The company plans to execute the additional 4 GW capacity in two phases of 2 GW each. The immediate focus is therefore on securing land in West Bengal and commencing construction while continuing to operate the existing cell and module lines at high utilisation. For investors, the next major milestones will be the completion of the land-allocation process, commencement of construction, equipment ordering and progress on the separate 150 MW TOPCon upgrade.

Websol management said the decision was primarily driven by the operating synergies it expects to derive from expanding around its existing manufacturing base in West Bengal.
The company has been operating in the state for more than three decades and believes the existing ecosystem can help it execute the next phase of capacity expansion more efficiently.

“We felt that doing it here we will be able to get the requisite synergies on account of supply chain, manpower, and just be able to execute faster in general,” Executive Director Sanjana Khaitan said during the call.
The company has clarified that its planned expansion is 4 GW in total and will be implemented in two phases of 2 GW each, rather than 4 GW each of cell and module capacity.
Management said the phased approach is intended to help manage technology and execution risks.
From Andhra Pradesh To Falta.
The proposed Phase 3 facility was earlier planned at Naidupeta in Andhra Pradesh.
There had been no financial outflow towards the Andhra Pradesh land, according to the company.
Websol said the preparatory work around the project, including the layout, equipment and identification of the team, had already been completed.
The company expects land approval during Q2 FY27, potentially in August.
Equipment ordering is planned around December, with machinery expected to reach the facility around April-May, followed by about two months of trial runs.
Websol has maintained that the shift in location should not change the broader project timeline.
“The capacity we have announced is what we are confident of executing.
Our project cost also remains the same, and the funding strategy and the pathway to that, which we have previously discussed also remains the same,” Khaitan said.
Cost And Operational Synergies.
The company expects the West Bengal location to provide both cost and operational benefits.
Management indicated that land-related expenditure is expected to be lower compared with Andhra Pradesh.
It also expects equipment costs to have declined over time, potentially reducing the overall project cost.
In addition, Websol expects to require fewer new employees, particularly at the senior level, because it can leverage skilled manpower already available at its existing facility.

“Establishing the expansion in our home state provides us with significant synergies in terms of infrastructure, availability of skilled manpower, supply chain and operational resources,” the company said.
The decision comes as Websol seeks to build its next phase of capacity around an existing manufacturing base rather than establish an entirely separate operating ecosystem.
Existing Cell, Module Capacity Runs.
At High Utilisation The location change also comes at a time when Websol’s existing cell and module manufacturing operations are operating at significantly higher utilisation.
In Q1 FY27, Websol produced 259 MW of solar cells compared with 126 MW in the year-ago quarter.
Cell utilisation reached 92%.
Module production more than doubled to 103 MW from 50 MW, while module utilisation increased to 81% from 39% a year earlier.
Management said both businesses are now operating close to full effective utilisation, although the TOPCon upgrade could result in some temporary downtime.
The higher utilisation translated into revenue from operations of ₹373 crore, up 70% year-on-year from ₹219 crore.
EBITDA increased 21% to ₹126 crore, while profit after tax rose 16% to ₹78 crore.
However, the increase in module production has changed Websol’s product mix.
Management said its objective is to operate the entire manufacturing base efficiently, grow absolute earnings and cash generation, and improve the economics of the business over time.
Demand Remains Strong.
In DCR Market Websol’s confidence in adding manufacturing capacity is also linked to its focus on the domestic content requirement market.

The company said its products are supplied largely to DCR projects, particularly those linked to the PM Surya Ghar and PM-KUSUM programmes, and that it is not currently seeing a reduction in demand from these segments.

Management also expects the broader solar market to continue expanding, citing emerging demand from artificial intelligence and data centres, battery energy storage systems and the growing requirement for solar-plus-storage capacity.
This demand outlook is supporting Websol’s confidence in scaling both its cell and module manufacturing operations.
₹1,278 Crore Order Book As of June 30, Websol had a confirmed order book of ₹1,278 crore, compared with ₹1,161 crore at the end of March 2026.
The company said this provides visibility into operations for the next few quarters.
Websol, however, only includes firm purchase orders in its disclosed order book.
The company does not count recurring business from customers that regularly purchase its products without entering into fixed-term contracts.
Management said it continues to receive regular inquiries for solar cells and modules in the DCR market and remains focused on producing and supplying to its regular customers.

The company also indicated that it has sufficient order visibility to sell the production it is generating, although the mix between cell and module sales can vary from quarter to quarter depending on realisations and market conditions.
TOPCon Upgrade Ahead Of Larger Expansion.
Before the larger greenfield expansion, Websol is upgrading one of its existing Mono PERC cell lines to TOPCon.
The upgrade will increase the line’s capacity from 600 MW to 750 MW, adding approximately 150 MW of capacity.
The project is expected to be completed by March 2027 and involves estimated capital expenditure of around ₹270 crore.
Management expects the investment to have a payback period of two to three years.
The company expects TOPCon to generate incremental revenue through higher wattage per cell, higher efficiency and higher realisation compared with Mono PERC.
Management said the wattage per cell could rise from around 7.6-7.7 Wp for its current Mono PERC cells to more than 9.5 Wp for TOPCon.

Websol also views the conversion as a learning exercise ahead of its larger greenfield expansion, giving the company practical experience in TOPCon technology before it ramps up the planned new capacity.
4 GW Expansion To Be Executed.
In Phases The larger expansion remains central to Websol’s growth strategy.
The company plans to execute the additional 4 GW capacity in two phases of 2 GW each.
The immediate focus is therefore on securing land in West Bengal and commencing construction while continuing to operate the existing cell and module lines at high utilisation.
For investors, the next major milestones will be the completion of the land-allocation process, commencement of construction, equipment ordering and progress on the separate 150 MW TOPCon upgrade.

stories.headline: BJP to hold Secretariat gherao on Aug 31 against 'misgovernance, corruption'
stories.title: BJP to hold Secretariat gherao on Aug 31 against 'misgovernance, corruption'
stories.summary: The Jammu and Kashmir unit of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has announced that it will hold a Secretariat Gherao outside the Civil Secretariat in Srinagar on August 31, accusing the National Conference-led government of failing on governance and alleging irregularities in appointments and corruption. According to BJP J&K Media Incharge Advocate Sajid Yousuf Shah, the party will mobilise its workers and supporters for the protest against what it described as the “misgovernance” of the NC government. The proposed protest is expected to focus on several issues, including alleged backdoor appointments, corruption and other governance-related concerns. The BJP is likely to use the protest to intensify its political campaign against the ruling National Conference government and highlight what it says are failures in administration and delivery of governance. The party said the Secretariat Gherao would be held on August 31 outside the Civil Secretariat in Srinagar, with BJP leaders and workers expected to participate in the demonstration. The announcement comes after the BJP had earlier planned a Secretariat Gherao March at Lal Chowk in Srinagar on July 20. However, the party had postponed the programme in view of the devastating flood situation in the border districts of Rajouri and Poonch. The BJP had said at the time that the decision to defer the protest was taken considering the prevailing situation in the affected areas and the need to prioritise relief and assistance amid the flood crisis. With the fresh announcement, the BJP has now decided to revive its protest programme and take its campaign directly to the seat of the Jammu and Kashmir government in Srinagar. The proposed mobilisation is also expected to bring renewed focus on the BJP’s criticism of the NC government over appointments and alleged corruption. The party has repeatedly raised allegations of favouritism and irregularities in government functioning, while the ruling party has maintained that its government is committed to transparent and accountable governance. The August 31 programme is likely to provide the BJP with a platform to further sharpen its political attack on the Omar Abdullah-led administration, particularly over issues of employment, recruitment, governance and alleged corruption. The BJP leadership is expected to spell out its demands and allegations in greater detail during the protest and call upon the government to address what it describes as major concerns affecting the people of Jammu and Kashmir. The proposed Secretariat Gherao will also be closely watched in view of its potential to escalate the political confrontation between the BJP and the National Conference government in the Union Territory.
